Thanks Hannah — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak TPS: our current target for Q4 pilot is ~120 TPS sustained over 10-minute windows, with spikes up to ~240 TPS for up to 3 minutes.
- Token mix: 90% short prompts (average 40 prompt tokens) and 10% long generations (avg 800 generated tokens). Average request size ~ 100 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p95 target 1200ms, p99 target 2200ms. We care more about p95 than absolute p50.
- Current infra: most of our training fleet uses A100 80GB but engineering is open to H100 evaluations. Procurement wants to understand cost delta between A100 pools vs A10G for inference.
- Security: we will likely need VPC peering + private endpoints (no public ingress) — so Dedicated in our VPC or Private deployment are both options; open to Redwood advice on ops tradeoffs.

I attached a token-profile CSV excerpt for the pilot day — hope that helps. Let us know if you need full traces.

—Emma

Emma — thanks for the numbers, very helpful. Quick technical notes and a couple of sizing heuristics based on the traffic profile you shared: 

1) GPU family tradeoffs (short):
   - A10G (Ampere): cost-efficient for high-concurrency short requests; memory 24–48GB variants are fine for smaller models or quantized weights. Good if you want aggressive price/perf.
   - A100 40/80GB: solid middle-ground — better large-model throughput and KV cache headroom; preferred if you keep full-precision or 8-bit quantization with larger context windows.
   - H100: best latency for heavy attention compute and FP16/FP8 optimization; higher cost but noticeably better p99 for long-generation bursts.

2) Concurrency & batching:
   - With 120 TPS sustained and average request ~100 tokens, a conservative Dedicated pool with 2–4 A100 80GB nodes (auto-scale with burst nodes) can meet p95 target if you enable small continuous batching (batch windows 5–10ms) and prefix KV caching for repeated prompts.
   - If Quantix prefers lower-cost steady-state, an A10G-dominant pool sized for concurrency (higher instance count) will reduce per-token cost but may increase tail latency on 800-token generations.

3) Token mix implications: your 10% long-generation fraction drives GPU memory and attention compute. We recommend reserving 1–2 nodes optimized for long jobs (H100 or A100 80GB) and the remainder for short, high-concurrency workers.

4) Private vs Dedicated:
   - Dedicated (Redwood-managed, dedicated GPU pool + VPC peering) gives fast time-to-pilot and our usual autoscaling.
   - Private (customer-managed on-prem / VPC private control plane) reduces surface for compliance but adds setup time and ops ownership. For pilot, Dedicated in your VPC is typically faster to stand up.

Attachments: I included a small token-profile example I used to sanity-check throughput — please find quantix_token_profile.csv attached. If you can share a 24h trace (anonymized), I can run a quick simulator and send back a recommended pool config.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated scenarios & quick cost/latency sketch

Emma / team — attached a short PDF with two concrete Dedicated sizing scenarios and a Hosted fallback: 

Scenario A (Low-latency / higher cost):
- Fleet: 3 x H100 nodes + 2 x A100 80GB for burst/long-gen offload
- Estimated steady-state: 140 TPS capacity, p95 ~ 900–1100ms, p99 ~ 1800–2100ms
- Recommended concurrency per node: 8–12 worker slots; small batching 5–10ms

Scenario B (Cost-optimized):
- Fleet: 6 x A10G + 1 x A100 80GB (long-gen reserve)
- Estimated steady-state: 120 TPS capacity, p95 ~ 1100–1500ms, p99 ~ 2400–3000ms (long-gen tails higher)
- Quantization: aggressive 4/8-bit where model quality allowed for short prompts

Hosted fallback: single larger Hosted instance for burst routing + Dedicated pool for steady traffic. Hosted keeps ops minimal but gives less isolation for keys/data.

Next steps I propose:
- Quantix to confirm which scenario you prefer (A or B) and whether you want a Private deployment evaluation.
- If you pick A/B, we’ll provision a pilot Dedicated pool for 2 weeks and run a soak with your token-profile.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-scenarios.pdf (2 pages)

Thanks — Marissa
